bottom_line: In high-risk patients, ramipril vs placebo reduced the primary composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes (relative risk, 0.78; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.70 to 0.86).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, ramipril reduced the risk of the primary composite endpoint versus placebo (0.78; 95% CI, 0.70–0.86) and also reduced all-cause death (0.84; 95% CI, 0.75–0.95). The results also show increased discontinuation for cough (7.3% vs 1.8%) and hypotension/dizziness (1.9% vs 1.5%). The document does not provide evidence here about effects in patients with heart failure or known low ejection fraction, who were excluded.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, two-by-two factorial trial; this report presents the placebo-controlled comparison of full-dose ramipril.
major_points.quote: The double-blind, two-by-two factorial, randomized Heart Outcomes Prevention Evaluation study evaluated ramipril and vitamin E

major_points.text: Population: 9297 high-risk patients aged 55 years or older with vascular disease or diabetes plus one other cardiovascular risk factor, without known low ejection fraction or heart failure.
major_points.quote: A total of 9297 high-risk patients (55 years of age or older) who had evidence of vascular disease or diabetes plus one other cardiovascular risk factor and who were not known to have a low ejection fraction or heart failure

major_points.text: Intervention: ramipril 10 mg once daily orally; comparator: matching placebo; mean follow-up five years.
major_points.quote: assigned to receive ramipril (10 mg once per day orally) or matching placebo for a mean of five years.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was lower with ramipril than placebo: 651 (14.0%) vs 826 (17.8%), relative risk 0.78 (95% CI, 0.70–0.86).
All-cause death was reduced with ramipril vs placebo: 482 (10.4%) vs 569 (12.2%), relative risk 0.84 (95% CI, 0.75–0.95).
Safety/tolerability: cough and hypotension/dizziness led to more stopping in the ramipril group than placebo.
major_points.quote: More patients in the ramipril group than in the placebo group stopped treatment because of cough (7.3 percent vs. 1.8 percent) or hypotension or dizziness (1.9 percent vs. 1.5 percent).

inclusion_criteria.text: Men and women at least 55 years old.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Men and women who were at least 55 years old were eligible for the study

inclusion_criteria.text: History of coronary artery disease, stroke, peripheral vascular disease, or diabetes plus at least one other cardiovascular risk factor.
inclusion_criteria.quote: eligible for the study if they had a history of coronary artery disease, stroke, peripheral vascular disease, or diabetes plus at least one other cardiovascular risk factor

exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were excluded if they had heart failure
Patients were excluded if they had heart failure, were known to have a low ejection fraction (<0.40)

exclusion_criteria.text: Taking an angiotensin-converting–enzyme inhibitor or vitamin E.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were excluded if they had heart failure, were known to have a low ejection fraction (<0.40), were taking an angiotensin-converting–enzyme inhibitor or vitamin E

Patients were excluded if they had heart failure, were known to have a low ejection fraction (<0.40), were taking an angiotensin-converting–enzyme inhibitor or vitamin E, had uncontrolled hypertension or overt nephropathy

exclusion_criteria.text: Myocardial infarction or stroke within four weeks before the study began.
exclusion_criteria.quote: or had had a myocardial infarction or stroke within four weeks before the study began.

baseline.characteristic: Aspirin or other antiplatelet agents — no. (%)

criticisms.text: Left ventricular function was not measured in all patients; only a substudy assessed it due to impracticality in this large trial.
criticisms.quote: In this large study it was impractical to measure left ventricular function in all patients.
